significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish both (i) that deceptive generation has a "linearly decodable signature in intermediate activations" and (iii) an ordering in which its probe generalizes across topics and elicitation methods "better than output-based lie detection." This is a representation-level phenomenon rather than a causal mechanism, but the cross-context performance relation would constrain whether monitoring should rely on internal activations rather than black-box signals—a material question given the concrete monitoring approaches in Burns et al. (ICLR 2023), Azaria and Mitchell (EMNLP Findings 2023), and Pacchiardi et al. (ICLR 2024). The branches are distinguishable: failure would rule out a transferable linear signature or its asserted advantage in the stated induced-deception setting, although it would not rule out nonlinear detectors or signatures of naturally emergent deception. In the topic-substitution check, generic mechanistic LLM safety would not preserve the specific cross-context and internal-versus-output ordering, so the score is attributable to the claim rather than the topic baseline.

reach.justification: The named handle is a "linear probe over intermediate activations" that distinguishes sincere from deceptive generation and can serve as an internal auditing diagnostic. Because activations are extracted "at the point of assertion," the handle is concurrent or post hoc rather than a forecast with substantial lead time, though an online system could potentially gate an assertion before release. The asserted relation travels across topics and elicitation methods and could inform deployment auditors, but after re-extraction on a new model it does not predict the new model's probe accuracy or robustness; scope is also limited by the claim's exclusion of naturally emergent deception and lack of an architecture-wide assertion. The topic-substitution check removes this specific probe, its cross-context transfer claim, and the activation-versus-output comparison, so the reach score is not credit for LLM safety in general.
